sentences.text: Using magnetoencephalography, a technique that measures magnetic fields generated by neural activity, researchers estimated the electrical power of synchronized brain activity in 30 people, finding an average of 6.6 × 10-9 watts.

The authors clarify that this figure reflects only the synchronized activity detectable by the scanner, not the brain's total energy use, noting that changes in the calculation method could alter the result by one to two orders of magnitude while remaining far below total metabolic energy.
In four example cases, the power lost to secondary currents was about 30% of the main power.
The patterns of electrical power found in the scans were linked to oxygen use and gene activity related to ketone metabolism, with varying effects across different brain networks.
